production.note: US model years, from J.D. Power's S4 model-year list (a database), which shows '2025, 2024, 2023, 2022, 2021, 2020, 2019, 2018, 2016' (no 2017: the B9 S4 arrived in the US as a 2018 model). Last: Edmunds (Steven Ewing, 16 July 2024): "Audi's long-running compact sedan will change its name from A4 to A5" (edmunds-a5-s5-first-look); the S5 sedan replaces the S4. No opened page states in so many words that 2025 was the last S4 model year.

body.note: '2019 Audi S4 Sedan'. The S4 Avant was not sold in the US.

configuration.note: '3.0-liter six-cylinder'; the brochure also says '3.0-liter TFSI® V6 engine'.

transmission.note: 'Eight-speed Tiptronic® automatic transmission', the only transmission.

powerHp.note: Quote: "Horsepower (@ rpm) ... 349 @ 5,400–6,400" (S4 column of the 2019 Audi A4/S4 US brochure; the same request twice gave 349). Launch-year rating: the 2018 S4 was rated 354 hp (automobile-catalog, a database: '2018 Audi S4 Specs Review (264 kW / 359 PS / 354 hp) ... for North America', autocatalog-s4-2018); from 2019 Audi rated it 349 hp, still listed for 2024 ('2024 Audi S4 ... 349 hp ... for North America', autocatalog-s4-2024). 349 hp covers 2019 to 2025, most of the run, so the reference year is 2019.

weightLb.note: Sedan with the 8-speed automatic (the only transmission), 2019 model. Quote: "Curb weight (lb) 3,450 3,627 3,825 3,858" (columns A4, A4 quattro, A4 allroad, S4).
